newsitem.title: IRAN: Malaysian official in Baghdad to expand trade ties.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian official in Baghdad to expand trade ties.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi was in Baghdad seeking sales under Iraq's oil-for-food deal and a role in developing Iraqi oilfields, diplomats and Iraqi officials said on Monday.
They said Badawi, leading a large delegation, was given a red-carpet welcome during the Moslem feast of Eid al-Adha, crowned with a meeting with Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein.
Baghdad newspapers quoted him telling Saddam he had "important talks with the Iraqi side during his official visit, discussing best ways to expand ties between Iraq and Malaysia in all fields."

The official Iraqi News Agency later said Badawi met Vice- President Taha Yassin Ramadan who told him that Saddam recommended "relations with Malaysia be strategic, varied and long term...in a manner realising the mutual benefits of the friendly peoples of the two countries."
Badawi, according to INA, said his country was keen to expand relations with Iraq, saying that the current visit would "end up in great results in the field of expanding bilateral relations."

Iraq relies on imports of Malaysian cooking oil. Iraq has allocated $111 million to buy cooking oil out of $1.3 billion it expects to get each six months from the oil-for-food deal allowed by the United Nations.

Badawi also met Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed, Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh and Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf. Malaysia's oil company Petronas is interested in the four billion barrel Ratawi oil field.
Iraq is under U.N. trade sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait but the oil-for-food deal is exempt from trade curbs.
